plugins.name: @kinetographdev/hexed
plugins.title: Hexed
plugins.description: Roll a look onto any picture or clip. Hexed picks a grade, a print screen, lens effects, tape damage and a camera shake. Keep the parts you like and reroll the rest.
plugins.intro: A look is eleven slots, each holding one named effect. Roll a number and every slot fills. The same number always gives the same look, so a render comes out the same every time.

features.title: Roll a look
features.text: One number picks a crop, a grade, a print screen, lens effects, tape damage and a camera shake. Roll again for a different look.

clip.caption: Rick Astley, with a new look rolled every second and a half.

features.title: Lock and reroll
features.text: Lock the slots you like and roll the rest again. Each label names the effects its number picked.

clip.caption: Twenty seeds rolled onto one frame, each with its effects named under it.

features.title: Saved looks
features.text: Save a look as a preset. Use it on the next video by name, and set how strong it is.

clip.caption: The moss-impact preset on the same footage.

exports.name: Hexed
exports.summary: Wraps any children and rolls a look onto them. It fills the composition unless you give a width and height.

studio.panel: Studio gets a Hexed panel: a card for each slot with its effect, a strength slider, a lock and a shuffle button. Shuffle rerolls everything except the locked slots, and a menu holds your presets. It follows Studio's light and dark theme.
studio.note: An agent can roll a look, list what each slot accepts and read your presets. It then writes the look it settles on into your code or saves it as a preset, so the look does not live only in Studio.
studio.installed: It installs as a package you add to your project. Its skill comes with it, so an agent can use it without being taught.

plugins.name: @kinetographdev/kinetic-typography
plugins.title: Kinetic typography
plugins.description: Captions that move with the voice, in fourteen ready-made styles. A hook word is set huge, and handwritten captions can follow a tracked subject.
plugins.intro: Captions sets a voiceover on screen. Each word arrives as it is said and the line leaves all together. A line with a big word is a hook: that word is set huge and the small words sit round it. HandCaptions writes the other way, one letter at a time in mixed handwriting.

features.title: Fourteen caption styles
features.text: Highlighter, typewriter, a text-selection sweep, a shine, a difference-blend prism and more. Pick one by name, then change its fonts, motion and colours. The accent colour and a readable shadow can come from your footage.

features.title: Hand captions
features.text: Each word writes itself across the time it is spoken, one letter at a time, every letter in a different handwritten face. Key words break out in a fat serif or a heavy italic, each with its own colour if you like. A dark halo keeps the letters readable over bright footage.

clip.caption: A line written centred low on archive film.

features.title: Follows a tracked subject
features.text: The text hangs beside the subject, on the side with room. A reticle frames the subject and a bracket marks the letter being written. Give it the subject's box and the text stays clear of it.

clip.caption: A line written beside a tracked anvil.

exports.name: HANDS
exports.summary: The default hands, mixed a letter at a time (OFL Google Fonts).

exports.name: HandCaptions
exports.summary: Captions written on in many hands, hanging off a tracked subject or centred low.

props.name: words
props.doc: The spoken words with their frames (wordsFrom turns timestamps in seconds into these).

props.name: split
props.doc: Words per page. Default 3 a page.

props.name: hot
props.doc: Words that break out in a display face: a word, or { word, color, face } to give it its own colour and face (serif or heavy; without one the faces take turns).

props.name: hotColor
props.doc: The colour of every hot word without its own. Default color.

props.name: anchor
props.doc: The tracked subject on a frame, in canvas pixels, or null where nothing is tracked: its centre, and its box (w, h) when known, which the reticle then frames and the text sits clear of. Without it the captions sit centred low in the frame, with no reticle or lines.

props.name: place
props.doc: Where the text hangs, when it should not follow the subject (a subject that jumps about, or a place kept clear of the picture): the lines still run to the subject. A box here keeps the text clear of it as anchor's does.

props.name: size
props.doc: Letter size, px. Default 124 at 1080 high, scaled with the canvas.

props.name: glow
props.doc: A CSS text-shadow for the glow, or '' for none.

props.name: halo
props.doc: A dark halo under the glow, so the letters read over bright footage and white flashes: true (strength 1) or a strength, 0..1.5. Default off.

props.name: fringe
props.doc: The pink and cyan fringe as letters land. Default true.

props.name: hands
props.doc: The hands mixed a letter at a time, and the two display faces.

props.name: doodle
props.doc: The doodle's colour beside a serif key word, or false for none.

props.name: reticle
props.doc: The reticle's label, or false for no reticle. Default TRK 01.

props.name: lines
props.doc: Lines from the subject to the text and off the frame. Default true.

props.name: top
props.doc: Highest the text block may reach, px from the top.

exports.name: SERIF
exports.summary: The display faces a key word breaks out in, taken in turn: a soft fat serif, and a heavy italic that streaks.

exports.name: haloOf
exports.summary: The dark halo, as text-shadows listed after the glow so they paint under it: a tight black edge round each letter, then darker and wider shadows, so whatever is behind a word falls to grey near it. k scales the opacities.

exports.name: pagesOf
exports.summary: The pages: split word counts per page (default 3 a page).
exports.detail: A page stays up until the next starts, or hold frames after its last word. hot words (compared without case or punctuation) break out, numbered by their place in hot.

exports.name: wordSpans
exports.summary: When each word is written: across its spoken time for a plain word, at once for one that breaks out.

exports.name: wordsFrom
exports.summary: Words from timestamps in seconds (an ASR or TTS word list), starting on frame at.

exports.name: Captions
exports.summary: Sets a voiceover on screen in one of fourteen ready-made styles. Each word arrives as it is said and the line leaves all together. A line with a big word is a hook.

props.name: words
props.doc: The spoken words with their frames (wordsFrom turns timestamps in seconds into these).

props.name: split
props.doc: Words per line. Default 3 a line.

props.name: big
props.doc: Words set big (matched without case or punctuation): a line with one is a hook.

props.name: marks
props.doc: Caption words marked out (heavier, coloured or boxed, by the look's mark). Default: each caption line's first word.

props.name: preset
props.doc: A style by name (STYLE_NAMES).

props.name: look
props.doc: Changes to the style, every line.

props.name: lines
props.doc: Changes for single lines, by line index from 0: { 2: { bigIn: 'left', big: { color: '#fff' } } }.

props.name: footage
props.doc: The video under the captions, timed as its <Video> is.

props.name: subject
props.type: (frame: number) => { x: number; y: number } | null
props.doc: The subject (a face) on a frame, in canvas pixels: beside puts the block in the open side of it, at its eye level. A point track from plugins/vj/tools/track.mjs read with pointAt, or a fixed point. Read once a line.

props.name: hold
props.doc: Frames a line stays after its last word when the next does not start sooner. Default 12.

exports.name: captionLines
exports.summary: The lines of a caption track: when each starts and ends and whether it is a hook (has a big word).

exports.name: checkFrames
exports.summary: Frames worth a still: a hook's big word and a caption line, each settled, to check that both read.

exports.name: ABOUT
exports.summary: One line on what each look is for, for the panel and for an agent choosing one.

exports.name: BASE
exports.summary: What every look starts from.

exports.name: FINISHES
exports.summary: The big word's surface: flat, a shine that sweeps across it, or a glow in its own colour.

exports.name: INS
exports.summary: How each word arrives. focus comes up from a blur; pop grows past its size and settles; typewriter and box-first are the moving styles used as an entrance for every word.

exports.name: LAYOUTS
exports.summary: Where the lines sit. over: the small words over and under the big word, upper middle. centre: the same block in the middle of the frame. left: flush left, upper left. beside: in the open side of the frame, at eye level (the side is read off the footage, or set). one-line: small and big words on one line. plain: captions only, the big word just marked.

exports.name: MARKS
exports.summary: How a caption word marks itself out (the line's marked word: marks, or its first word).

exports.name: OUTS
exports.summary: How a line leaves, all its words together.

exports.name: STYLES
exports.summary: The fourteen ready-made styles, by name.
exports.detail: Each is a patch on BASE.

exports.name: TREATMENTS
exports.summary: How the big word is dressed as it arrives. box-first: a box grows, then the word lands in it. typewriter: typed a letter at a time with a cursor. select: a blue text selection sweeps across it. highlight: a colour sweeps in behind it, like a highlighter pen. underline: a bar draws under it.

exports.name: resolveLook
exports.summary: BASE, then a style, then patches in order; caption and big merge field by field.

exports.name: styleLook
exports.summary: A look by style name, with overrides.

exports.name: accentFrom
exports.summary: An accent colour taken from the footage: the strongest hue across a few moments of it (each cell weighted by how saturated and lit it is, so a lamp or a shirt wins over a grey wall), lifted to a colour that reads behind or as white-on text. fallback when the footage has no colour (black and white film).

exports.name: brightness
exports.summary: Mean brightness 0..1 of the picture in a box given as fractions of the frame [x0, y0, x1, y1].

exports.name: openSide
exports.summary: The side of the frame with less going on (less contrast between neighbouring cells), between y0 and y1.

exports.name: subjectFrom
exports.summary: The subject's head from a matte (white subject on black, timed like the footage): the middle of the matte's top band across, and eye level a little under its top.
exports.detail: For <Captions subject>, so beside stays clear of a subject who moves. Null where the matte is empty.

exports.name: timeAt
exports.summary: Seconds into the file at composition frame frame.

exports.name: captionLookSchema
exports.summary: A caption look: style names a ready-made look, the rest change it.
exports.detail: Every field is optional.

exports.name: captionsSchema
exports.summary: <Captions>'s props, for a composition whose schema is the component's.

exports.name: textLookSchema
exports.summary: One kind of text, the caption or the big text.

examples.title: Captions in a ready-made style
Hand captions from word timestamps
Hung off a tracked subject

studio.panel: Studio gets a Captions panel: a card for each style drawn in its own type, a Caption or Big text switch for font, case, weight, size, tracking and colour, layout cards, motion controls with an In and Out switch, and an accent colour you can take from the footage. Hook and Caption pins sit on the preview and you drag them up or down. HandCaptions has no panel.
studio.note: There are no agent tools. The skill tells an agent to take word timestamps from your speech-to-text or voice-over tool instead of placing frames by hand, choose the lines and the big words, and render a settled hook frame and caption frame to check that both read. For tracked text it tracks the subject with the VJ plugin.
studio.installed: It installs as a package you add to your project. Its skill comes with it, so an agent can use it without being taught.

plugins.name: @kinetographdev/paper
plugins.title: Paper
plugins.description: Give a video the feel of real paper. Keyword match cuts, photo cut-outs that unfold from a crumpled packet, and hand-drawn lines round a moving subject on torn paper.
plugins.intro: Paper brings creases, scanned fibres and grain to a video. From them it makes keyword match cuts, photo cut-outs and hand-drawn lines on torn paper.

features.title: MatchCut
features.text: A highlighted keyword holds still while the page under it changes several times a second. Use made-up pages or your own screenshots.

clip.caption: The web look, keyword Super Bowl.

features.title: CutOut and FoldOut
features.text: A photo with its background removed becomes a paper cut-out. FoldOut opens it from a crumpled packet, in stop motion.

clip.caption: A cut-out opening on a desk.

features.title: Scrapline
features.text: A marker, pencil, crayon, scribble or brush line is drawn round a moving subject, on torn paper. It redraws a few times a second, like hand animation.

clip.caption: A crayon line on binder paper round a moving subject.

exports.name: MatchCut
exports.summary: A keyword holds still, highlighted, while the page under it changes several times a second. It fills its composition.

props.name: preset
props.doc: a look by name from presets/, under look

props.name: everyNth
props.doc: a screenshot every nth cut (1: screenshots only); made-up pages between

props.name: seed
props.doc: another pile of made-up pages

props.name: showKeyBox
props.doc: draw the hint (blue) and the snapped box (red) on screenshots, to check them in a still

props.name: durationInFrames
props.doc: frames the push-in runs over; default the composition's

exports.name: cutOf
exports.summary: The cut showing at frame, for sound or for cutting to something else on a cut.

exports.name: Paper
exports.summary: The sheet: a tint, crumpled creases, a scan multiplied over it if one is given (texture, a path under public/, stretched to cover), a soft fall-off to the corners. seed picks the crumple.

exports.name: focus
exports.summary: Sharp on a band round the line y = ay, softer with distance above and below it (full blur falloff bands out), the blur smear times taller than wide there so copy runs into vertical streaks; past side from the middle the blur also streaks sideways.
exports.detail: Each pixel gathers 24 points on a spiral sized by its own blur.

exports.name: measure
exports.summary: The advance of text in face at size px, measured once at 100 px on an OffscreenCanvas.

exports.name: screen
exports.summary: The page as a filmed screen: the picture broken into pixel-px cells, each lit as three soft RGB stripes with a dark gap between rows (an LCD's subpixels, close up), a slight barrel from the lens (curve, filling the frame), and a soft fall-off to the corners. amount 0..1 mixes it in.
exports.detail: Screen space, so the grid holds still under a push-in, as the monitor does in front of a camera.

exports.name: PAGE_LAYOUTS
exports.summary: Printed and article pages: what a look uses when it names no layouts.
exports.detail: The social pages (tweet, reddit, comments) are screens, so a look picks them on purpose (the web preset does).

exports.name: SCREEN_LAYOUTS
exports.summary: Layouts that are app screens: they keep their own background (light or dark mode), whatever the look's tint.

exports.name: page
exports.summary: Page n for keyword, made from layouts in turn from a shuffled start so neighbours differ. reach is how far the copy must run above, below and to each side, page pixels; seed gives another pile of pages.

exports.name: snapBox
exports.summary: The keyword's exact box near hint in the image at src (a resolved URL or path), image pixels.
exports.detail: The hint is returned as it is when no ink is found.

exports.name: crinkle
exports.summary: Paper crumpled or opened: a dense burst of crackles (each a millisecond or so of noise, loudness spread like real crumpling: mostly faint, now and then a loud snap) over a soft rustle, length seconds long.
exports.detail: Built sample by sample into one buffer from random(key), then shaped: high-passed, a papery presence lift.

exports.name: flick
exports.summary: A page flicked over: a short burst of bright noise with a papery band, key varying each one.

exports.name: flicks
exports.summary: A flick on every cut: cuts begin at frame start and come cutsPerSecond a second for frames frames.

exports.name: land
exports.summary: A sheet landing flat on a desk: a soft low thump of air and paper, with a few crackles on top.

exports.name: unfolds
exports.summary: The sound of a <FoldOut>: a crinkle on each stop-motion step while it opens (louder as the flaps get bigger), then the sheet landing flat.
exports.detail: Pass the FoldOut's delay, duration and steps (defaults the same: 0, 0.7 s, 10), and start, the composition frame its Sequence starts on.

plugins.name: @kinetographdev/vj
plugins.title: VJ
plugins.description: Make footage look like a CRT, a worn VHS tape, a thermal camera or a 1-bit screen. Track what moves and draw boxes on it, cut a person into a pop-art poster, or fly a camera through clips seen as windows.
plugins.intro: VJ makes a picture look like it came from a screen, a tape or a sensor. Brightness stands in for heat and depth, so these are looks, not measurements. It also draws tracking marks on whatever moves, cuts a person into a pop-art poster and builds a camera fly-through of clips.

features.title: Screens and tapes
features.text: A CRT with curved glass that switches off, a worn VHS tape, a 1-bit screen, and a pixel magnifier that resolves into red, green and blue stripes.

clip.caption: A CRT tube switching off, on archive film.

features.title: Thermal and depth
features.text: Brightness becomes a thermal-camera palette or a depth-map look.

clip.caption: A thermal palette over a parade.

features.title: Flash looks
features.text: Acid heat, night vision, screen glow and grainy black and white, to cut on the beat.

clip.caption: Flash looks on a song, each held for a second and a half.

features.title: PopArt
features.text: Footage of a person cuts to an anime poster of them: blue tones, ink lines and rim light over a halftone. It needs a matte of the person, which a bundled tool makes once per clip.

clip.caption: Fred Ott cut to an anime poster and back.

features.title: Tracking
features.text: A tracker runs once and saves where things moved. Blobs draws boxes and links on every frame. Reticle marks one point.

features.title: Fragments
features.text: Clips show only through windows: boxes round the people and animals in them, tiles of sky, round holes. Each clip sits on its own plane at its own depth, and a camera flies through so near pieces slide past faster than far ones. Boxes carry name tags with a flickering confidence figure. Whoever edits the video names the boxes; no detection model runs.

exports.name: IRON
exports.summary: A thermal camera's palette (iron: cold violet through red to white-hot), a little soft as such sensors are.

exports.name: RAINBOW
exports.summary: The other common one: cold blue through green to hot red and white.

exports.name: crt
exports.summary: A colour tube: curved glass, scanlines, aperture grille, misconvergence, a rolling bar, static and dark corners.

props.name: cx
props.doc: The tube face's centre and half-size on the canvas, px. The default is the whole layer.

props.name: curve
props.doc: How far the glass bends. 0 is flat.

props.name: pitch
props.doc: Source pixels per scanline.

props.name: scan
props.doc: 0..1: how dark between the lines.

props.name: grille
props.doc: Screen pixels per grille stripe.

props.name: mask
props.doc: 0..1: how strong the grille is.

props.name: conv
props.doc: Pixels the red and blue guns land off green.

props.name: offx
props.doc: 1 is on. Switching off: offy falls to 0 first (a line), then offx (a dot).

exports.name: depthLook
exports.summary: A depth map's look: near is white, far is black, smooth, no texture.
exports.detail: Brightness stands in for nearness.

exports.name: lookEffects
exports.summary: The effects for a vjLookSchema value (from the Studio panel): <Layer effects={lookEffects(look)}>.

exports.name: oneBit
exports.summary: One bit a pixel: grey, hard contrast, an ordered dither in cells of size px, printed in ink on paper.

exports.name: pixels
exports.summary: A magnifier: blocks, then red, green and blue subpixel stripes as the zoom grows.

exports.name: switchOff
exports.summary: The tube switching off over t 0..1, as crt()'s offx and offy: the picture folds to a bright line over the first 60%, and the line to a dot over the rest.
exports.detail: Spread it into the options: crt({ ...switchOff(t) }).

exports.name: thermal
exports.summary: A thermal camera's palette on the picture's brightness, a little soft.

exports.name: vhs
exports.summary: A worn tape: line wobble, late smeared colour, a head-switch tear, a drifting tracking band, snow and dropouts.

props.name: trackAt
props.doc: 0..1: where the tracking band is, top to bottom.

props.name: trackW
props.doc: Half-height of the band, px.

props.name: track
props.doc: 0..1: how bad the tracking is.

props.name: bleed
props.doc: How wide the colour smears, px, and how late it lands.

props.name: drops
props.doc: 0..1: chance per line per frame of a dropout.

exports.name: FLASH_OVERLAY
exports.summary: Which screen-glow variants lay an overlay on (screen blend), and how strongly.
exports.detail: The overlay is the caller's.

exports.name: acid
exports.summary: Brightness to hue: from hue (degrees) round the colour wheel cycles times (negative runs the other way) as the picture brightens, gamma under 1 spending more of the turn on the shadows, at full saturation, the brightest parts washed to white: the acid heat camera.

exports.name: adaptiveCut
exports.summary: A hard black and white cut that follows the footage: each pixel is cut against the mean brightness of a wide patch round it (reach, a fraction of the frame height), times bias, so bright footage and dark footage both split into big black and white shapes instead of going all white or all black.

exports.name: acidHeat
exports.summary: Acid heat camera.
exports.detail: 1 and 4 soft blobs, folded; 2 sharp, warm shadows; 3 sharp, teal shadows.

exports.name: fold
exports.summary: One half folded onto the other. axis 0: left onto right, 1: top onto bottom. box is the picture on the canvas ([x, y, w, h], px); without it, the whole canvas.

exports.name: grainyBW
exports.summary: Grainy black and white.
exports.detail: 1 soft and high-key, 5 high-key with grain; 2-4 a hard cut that follows the footage's brightness (3 and 4 folded), 6 the cut smeared down.

exports.name: nightVision
exports.summary: Night vision: lime phosphor with lifted blacks, a little noise.
exports.detail: 1-5 smeared by the camera's move, 6 still.

exports.name: screenGlow
exports.summary: Screen glow: the picture's own colours pushed bright and blue-cyan into a big bloom.
exports.detail: 1-3 bright (3 soft), 7 deep blue and crushed, 8 nearly clean, a little cool; 4-6 are 1 with room for an overlay (FLASH_OVERLAY).

exports.name: streak
exports.summary: A blur along one direction (degrees), as a fast pan or a shake smears it.

exports.name: PopArt
exports.summary: The pop-art cut-in on any clip of a person.
exports.detail: Place it in a <Sequence> to start the clip later.

props.name: src
props.doc: the clip of the person

props.name: matte
props.doc: its person matte (white = person), from tools/matte.mjs

props.name: track
props.doc: where the person is on every frame, from tools/matte.mjs --track; without it the rays start mid-frame

props.name: rate
props.doc: the clip's playback rate

props.name: cuts
props.doc: when to cut to the poster; without cuts the poster is on throughout

props.name: flash
props.doc: frames that flash to a single yellow card

props.name: title
props.type: { kicker: string; line1: string; line2: string } | null
props.doc: the three title rows; null for none

props.name: chest
props.doc: how far below the person's centre the rays and shapes start, px (1920x1080 space)

props.name: id
props.doc: a prefix for the layer ids, unique per <PopArt> on screen

exports.name: Blobs
exports.summary: Boxes, labels and links on a tracked clip's blobs.
exports.detail: Put it over the clip, the same size.

props.name: from
props.doc: The composition frame the tracked clip starts on. Default 0.

props.name: width
props.doc: The overlay's size: the clip's picture, filling it. Default the composition's.

props.name: box
props.doc: How each blob is marked: a full box, the box's corners, a cross on its centre, or nothing. Default frame.

props.name: label
props.doc: The text beside each box: its id, its centre as 0..1 coordinates, both, or nothing. Default both.

props.name: reach
props.doc: For links="all": how far apart two blobs may be and still be linked, as a fraction of the diagonal.

props.name: invert
props.doc: 0..1: the share of blobs (picked by id) filled solid in difference blending, inverting the picture under them.

props.name: min
props.doc: Blobs smaller than this fraction of the frame are left out.

props.name: max
props.doc: The biggest this many are kept.

props.name: blend
props.doc: How the boxes, lines and labels sit on the picture. difference keeps them readable on white and black alike (a 1-bit picture); normal keeps color as it is. Default normal.

props.name: stroke
props.doc: Line width, px.

props.name: id
props.doc: Prefix of the layer ids.

exports.name: blobsAt
exports.summary: The blobs on composition frame frame (at fps) of a clip that starts on frame from, scaled to width x height.
exports.detail: The track may run at another rate than the composition: it is read by time. Past the clip's end: none.

exports.name: Fragments
exports.summary: Clips seen through windows on planes at different depths, with a camera moving through them.

props.name: camera
props.type: CameraKey[] | ((frame: number) => { x: number; y: number; z: number })
props.doc: Keys the camera eases between (x, y in px, z in depth units), or a function of the frame. Default: a slow push from z 0 to 0.5 over the composition.

props.name: colors
props.doc: Colours of the tags by name; other names get one from a set, the same each time.

props.name: fontSize
props.doc: Tag text size, clip px. Default 22.

props.name: fog
props.doc: 0..1: how much a piece dims per unit of depth past 1. Default 0.25.

props.name: inspect
props.doc: Show piece inspect flat, whole and filling the frame, at its clip's own frame (its from ignored), with every box's id, every spot's name and a grid in clip pixels: render stills of it to name the ids and place spots.

exports.name: cameraAt
exports.summary: The camera on frame: eased between the keys, held before the first and after the last.

props.name: camera
props.type: CameraKey[] | ((frame: number) => { x: number; y: number; z: number })
props.doc: Keys the camera eases between (x, y in px, z in depth units), or a function of the frame. Default: a slow push from z 0 to 0.5 over the composition.

props.name: colors
props.doc: Colours of the tags by name; other names get one from a set, the same each time.

props.name: fontSize
props.doc: Tag text size, clip px. Default 22.

props.name: fog
props.doc: 0..1: how much a piece dims per unit of depth past 1. Default 0.25.

props.name: inspect
props.doc: Show piece inspect flat, whole and filling the frame, at its clip's own frame (its from ignored), with every box's id, every spot's name and a grid in clip pixels: render stills of it to name the ids and place spots.

exports.name: Reticle
exports.summary: A box with corner ticks and a label, on the tracked point.

props.name: size
props.doc: The box's side, px.

props.name: label
props.doc: The text under the box. A confidence figure flickers beside it.

props.name: jitter
props.doc: px the box shakes by each frame, as a lock that is never quite still.

exports.name: pointAt
exports.summary: The tracked point on composition frame frame (at fps) of a clip that starts on from, scaled to width x height; held at the first or last point outside the clip.

exports.name: LOOK_KINDS
exports.summary: The looks lookEffects knows, none included.

exports.name: blobStyleSchema
exports.summary: How <Blobs> marks the blobs: its props other than the track.
exports.detail: Spread it into <Blobs>.

exports.name: vjLookSchema
exports.summary: One look and the settings of each, so switching looks keeps what was set on the others.

examples.title: A look and tracked boxes over a clip
Track once, offline, then draw
examples.code:
# finds what moved since the last frame; --debug writes every 10th frame with its boxes
node plugins/vj/tools/blobs.mjs --in public/clip.mp4 --out track/clip-blobs.json --debug out/blobs

# follows one patch (x, y, w, h on the first frame)
node plugins/vj/tools/track.mjs --in public/clip.mp4 --box 900,300,120,120 --out track/clip-point.json

studio.panel: Studio gets a VJ panel with a card for each look and that look's own sliders and colours. Switching looks keeps the settings of the others. On the preview you drag and resize the CRT screen and drag the magnifier's centre. A second panel sets how the tracking marks look: box style, labels, links, blend, how many blobs to show, line width and colour.
studio.note: Tracking runs on your own machine ahead of time, so the panel only styles the result. The plugin adds no agent tools. The skill walks an agent through tracking a clip, checking the debug images, tuning the tracker and rendering a still to check. For Fragments it has the agent name the boxes from stills of each clip.
studio.installed: It installs as a package you add to your project. Its skill comes with it, so an agent can use it without being taught.

clips.caption: PopArt: Fred Ott cut to an anime poster and back.
Thermal: a parade in thermal colour.

looks.summary: A colour tube: curved glass, scanlines, aperture grille, misconvergence, a rolling bar, static and dark corners.
A worn tape: line wobble, late smeared colour, a head-switch tear, a drifting tracking band, snow and dropouts.
One bit a pixel: grey, hard contrast, an ordered dither in cells of size px, printed in ink on paper.
A thermal camera's palette on the picture's brightness, a little soft.
A depth map's look: near is white, far is black, smooth, no texture.
A magnifier: blocks, then red, green and blue subpixel stripes as the zoom grows.
Screen glow: the picture's own colours pushed bright and blue-cyan into a big bloom.
Night vision: lime phosphor with lifted blacks, a little noise.

components.title: Screenshot card burst
components.description: A wordmark fades in on black, then a cluster of screenshot cards bursts out of one point as the camera flies in. The cards settle into a dense wall, drift, and whip off to the right. Big white type finishes it: two short lines, each starting as a single word.
change: The brand name and the word after it in the wordmark (or none), and the two closing lines.
Your own screenshots or photos on the cards, and the words printed on the cards. With none, every card is drawn.
The three typefaces (wordmark and cards, terminal, serif) and the colours: canvas, text, accent, paper and dark cards.
The seed, which sets the tilt and timing of the burst.

components.title: App window greeting
components.description: A gradient wordmark on a soft off-white ground shrinks away as an app window grows in behind it. The camera pushes into the window, tilted, and types a greeting and a question in large perspective type. Four suggestion cards slide in, then the camera pulls back and flattens to the whole window.
change: The brand name, the name in the greeting, the question under it and the placeholder in the prompt box.
One to four suggestion cards, with your own labels, and the small caption at the bottom (or none).
The typeface, and the colours: ground, glows, window, cards, text and the wordmark and greeting gradients.
Whether it moves in two-frame steps or smoothly at 60 frames a second.

components.title: Social post on a phone
components.description: A phone showing a social post starts as a close-up of its lower edge, pulls back and glides to rest. Chat bubbles, avatars and icon chips pop in around it. A hand reaches into the photo and lifts the phone, and the screen swaps to a second one as the view count reaches its cap.
change: The brand name in the post header, the caption pill and the two-part subtitle on the photo.
The view count: where it starts, where it stops, and its unit.
The three chat bubbles, and the words on the second screen.
Your own photo for the post, a second picture for the swap, a logo and four avatars. Without them, all of it is drawn.
The typefaces and colours, and whether the motion steps at 24 frames a second or runs smooth at 60.

components.title: Chat prompt to reply
components.description: A chat prompt types itself into a rounded box and sends. The shot cuts to the reply, built on a page the camera scrolls through. Two activity rows, a status line, a serif reply, a brand chip, a small table and a row of action icons fade up one after another.
change: The prompt, the two activity rows, the status line and the reply.
The brand chip, and the table: three column heads and one row.
The three typefaces (interface, mono chip, serif reply).
The colours: background, panel, text, the warm typing tint, labels, links and icons.

components.title: Scrapline cut-outs
components.description: A hand-drawn border round a cut-out subject, on a sheet of torn paper. The line can be a wobbly marker, pencil, crayon, scribble or brush. Line and paper redraw a few times a second, like hand animation.
change: The subject: a video with a black and white matte, a video with alpha, an image with alpha, or an SVG path.
The line style (Marker, Pencil, Crayon, Scribble or Brush), the paper (White, Kraft, Binder, Cardboard, your own picture or none), the line colour, the gap to the subject and the seed.

components.title: Two lines on a focus pull
components.description: Seven photo cards float round the edges of a near-black frame, out of focus. The camera pulls back and racks focus. A first line comes up out of the blur and a second line replaces it. The scene slides off to the right as the left card sharpens.
change: The two lines, and a product name in the second.
Your own photos on the seven cards. Any card you leave out keeps its drawn picture.
The typeface, weight, size, tracking and text colour, and the two colours of the background.
How strong the focus blur, the film grain and the closing slide are, and the frame where the first line gives way to the second.

components.title: Words cut to the beat
components.description: A 9.4 second black-and-white type spot, cut on every hit of its track. Each cut shows one word or a two-word lockup on a ground that flips between black and white. A last word types on, then blurs away.
change: The words: an intro, a run with one word per cut, and an outro. The word count has to match the number of cuts.
The track. A small tool finds its strongest hits and gives you the cuts.
The typeface. Another face lands in the same places.
